messages:
incident-bot: Pager: runtime queue depth spike in us-west-2 (p99 queue depth > 1200ms). Alerting 1/2 oncall. see: https://obs.redwood/alerts/4791122334
sara (oncall): Looking. Seeing rapid increase in tail latency on embed-production workers, queueing at router layer. stack traces show inflight growth.
mike: Any recent deploys to that fleet?
sara (oncall): No deploys in last 30m. Autoscaler not keeping up with short CPU bursts.
jordan: Can you run the quick-query? `SELECT count(*) FROM inflight WHERE region='us-west-2' AND age>30s`
sara (oncall): Ran it — returns ~320 inflight long requests, threshold 50. Most for model: redwood-embed-xl with seq_len 2048.
nina: Customer impact? Which customers are hitting those big sequences?
sara (oncall): Top callers: acme-inc, spacechat, two internal test accounts. acme is heavy, but not fully degraded — requests queued >5s. We should decide mitigation ASAP before throttling.
sara (oncall): Proposed mitigations: 1) enable soft-shedding for embed-production (max_inflight -> 200) 2) temporarily disable batch-embedding API param "max_sequence" for public tier 3) apply per-customer short quota bump for enterprise accounts (acme) to avoid errors while we scale. Thoughts?
mike: +1 for soft-shedding. We should not shut down embeddings completely. Start with shedding and timeout tuning (reduce default worker timeout from 120s -> 40s)
jordan: Agreed. Also route new requests to us-east-1 via smart-routing if acceptable. That buys headroom.
sara (oncall): Taking actions now: 1) `curl -XPOST https://control.redwood/api/runtime/config -d '{"path":"/services/embed-production/max_inflight","value":200}'` 2) `curl -XPOST https://control.redwood/api/runtime/config -d '{"path":"/services/embed-production/worker_timeout_s","value":40}'` 3) `POST /ops/quota/adjust` for acme +20% for 2h.
incident-bot: Deploy task queued: cfg-update-77912 started by sara (oncall). Audit id: cfg-77912
sara (oncall): Done pushing max_inflight and timeout. Applying soft-shedding flag: `sh ./tools/set_shed.sh embed-prod soft`
mike: I pushed a temporary token-bucket throttle for public tier: per-ip rps -> 10, per-api-key concurrency -> 4. Will revert after we confirm.
sara (oncall): Observability: p99 queue depth down from 1200ms -> 320ms in 2m, inflight long requests dropped from 320 -> 90. Good signal.
nina: Can we pause response-streaming for large sequences? That's another heavy path.
sara (oncall): Yes — toggling `response.streaming=off` for embed-production for public tier now.
sara (oncall): Notified support to prepare customer comms for acme and spacechat — telling them temporary performance hiccup and we've applied short quota bump.
sam (prod): Heads up — I've also routed a small % of new traffic to a cold pool with extra quantized replicas (q4) to handle long sequences.
jordan: Nice. Keep monitoring for regressions. If p95 > 2s for next 10m we should consider enabling canary autoscale (add 8 gpus) or manual capacity bump.
sara (oncall): We'll wait 10m. Current plan: monitor 10m -> if stable, leave soft-shedding + throttles + timeout. If not, escalate to infra for capacity.
mike: If we end up adding capacity, coordinate with infra first — we might need to rebalance shards.
sara (oncall): Logging handoff: Oncall-> night-team at 4791122380. Mitigations in place: soft-shedding=true, worker_timeout_s=40, per-tier throttles set, response-streaming disabled for large seq, acme quota bump +20% for 2h, partial routing to q4 replicas.
jordan: I'll follow through on capacity if needed.
nina: I'll draft a brief update to acme support and PM.
sara (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated for now. Monitoring window open for 30m. If anything changes ping @sara or escalate to pager. :thumbsup:
